/** Generate a fiscal year's monthly periods: how many were made, or null when refused. */
export async function generateFy(page: Page, year: string): Promise<number | null> {
  await page.getByTestId('period-generate-fy-year').fill(year);
  const was = await shown(page.getByTestId('period-generated'));
  await page.getByTestId('period-generate-fy').click();
  const n = await countAfter(page, page.getByTestId('period-generated'), page.getByTestId('period-generate-error'), 'generate fiscal year', was);
  return n === null ? null : Number(n);
}

/** Search the tree: the result lines in order, once the screen says how many there are. */
export async function search(page: Page, text: string): Promise<string[]> {
  await page.getByTestId('search-name').fill(text);
  await page.getByTestId('search').click();
  const count = page.getByTestId('search-count');
  await expect.poll(async () => {
    const n = await shown(count);
    return n !== '' && Number(n) === (await page.getByTestId('search-line').count());
  }, { timeout: WAIT }).toBe(true);
  return (await page.getByTestId('search-line').allTextContents()).map((t) => t.trim());
}

export async function exportClaims(page: Page): Promise<string> {
  const [download] = await Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('download'), page.getByTestId('export-claims').click()]);

The tree search is in: a box and a button on the sheet list everyone in this sheet's tree whose name or alias contains the typed text, ignoring case. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

Each result line reads `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`. This sheet's people come first in list order, then the other sheets' by sheet id. The due-total is the same figure the person's row shows, or `n/a`.

**Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree` (`rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree.GET.yml` and `sheet/RespondWithTree.java`), returns the ids of the other sheets in the tree, sorted. It reuses `PersonRepository.treeOf`, the same tree the rule that names must be unique across a tree already uses: parents going up and children going down.

**Front end:** the panel is in `features/search/search.slot.tsx`. It works like the consolidated-figures panel: it loads each sheet's people and claims and uses the existing due-total calculation. The test ids are `search-name`, `search`, `search-count` and `search-line`, plus `search-error` if the tree can't be read.

How it behaves in cases the spec doesn't cover:
- **Sibling sheets are left out.** The search covers the sheet's ancestors and descendants, not other branches under a shared parent. Claim numbering uses a wider tree (the top sheet and everything below it), so say if you want the search to use that one instead.
- **Retired people are included,** whether or not "show retired" is on, the same as the people export.
- **Each press reads every sheet fresh, as it stands now.** That means the results ignore any "as of" date the screen is set to, the same as the consolidated figures. The count stays blank until every sheet has been read.
